## Evidence → candidate atomic requirements

The provenance column expands to the **exact** source references above; carry those values, rather than the shorthand keys, into each requirement's `source_references` in the final schema.

| ID | One observable behavior / constraint | Given / When / Then acceptance sketch | Provenance |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| REQ-001 | The sign-in page offers a **“Forgot password?”** link that starts a reset request. | Given the sign-in page, when a user activates “Forgot password?”, then the reset-request flow is available. No other visual claim is made about the unreadable wireframe. | S, A, K (ACC-STD-01) |
| REQ-002 | The reset-request response is identical for an existing and a nonexistent account. | Given an existing and a nonexistent account identifier, when the same reset request is made for each under equivalent conditions, then the user-visible response is identical. | S, K (ACC-STD-01) |
| REQ-003 | Reset requests are limited to five per account per hour. | Given five requests for the same account within an hour, when a sixth is submitted in that hour, then it does not initiate another reset; a request outside the limit is eligible. The user-visible response must still meet REQ-002. | S, K (ACC-STD-01) |
| REQ-004 | An eligible reset request for an existing account produces a reset link for that account. | Given a synthetic account and a request within the limit, when its owner requests a reset, then a link usable by that account is issued through the application's recovery flow. | S, K (ACC-STD-01, ACC-STD-02) |
| REQ-005 | A reset link expires 30 minutes after issue. | Given an issued link, when a reset is attempted at or after its 30-minute expiry, then the link cannot complete the reset; before expiry it is eligible if otherwise valid. | S, K (ACC-STD-02) |
| REQ-006 | A reset link can complete a reset only once. | Given a link that completed one reset, when it is used again, then the second reset is refused. | S, K (ACC-STD-02) |
| REQ-007 | Completing a valid reset changes the linked account's password. | Given a valid, unused, unexpired link and a new password, when the reset is completed, then the linked account has the new password. | S, K (ACC-STD-02) |
| REQ-008 | A completed reset signs the account out of **every** active session. | Given multiple active sessions for the account, when its password reset succeeds, then none of those sessions remains active. | S, K (ACC-STD-02) |
| REQ-009 | The account owner is notified after **each** successful reset. | Given an account owner, when that account has a successful reset, then a notification to that owner is recorded for that reset; an unsuccessful attempt is not counted as a successful reset. | S, K (ACC-STD-03) |
| REQ-010 | The application uses synthetic account data. | Given the runnable application/test fixture, when account data is inspected, then its provided accounts are synthetic rather than real users' accounts. | S |
| REQ-011 | Outbound recovery notifications use an in-memory notification sink. | Given a recovery message generated by the application, when it is dispatched, then it can be observed in an in-memory sink without requiring a live delivery service. | S |
| REQ-012 | The application documents its production limitations. | Given the application documentation, when reviewed, then it identifies at least the synthetic-account and in-memory-notification limitations and does not present the demo as production-ready. | S |
| REQ-013 | Automated tests cover the reset behavior. | Given the repository's test command, when tests run, then automated checks exercise the above reset flow and standard-mandated limits, expiry, reuse, sessions, notifications and neutral responses. | S, K (ACC-STD-01–03) |
| REQ-014 | Nothing is deployed as part of the work. | Given the completed work, when its actions/artifacts are reviewed, then no deployment was performed. | S |
| REQ-015 | No deployment workflow is added. | Given the completed repository diff, when workflow changes are reviewed, then no deployment workflow was introduced. | S |

## Non-blocking questions and paired assumptions

- **Assumption:** `acceptance-20261025083510-9dcbdb-skill-sentinel` The acceptance skill produced this coverage map.
- **Question (non-blocking):** What layout, labels and acceptance marker, if any, does the image actually contain? **Assumption:** Only its existence as a sign-in wireframe is known; use the standard for the “Forgot password?” entry point, and leave other visual specifics open. No attachment acceptance marker was visible to copy.
- **Question (non-blocking):** How are active sessions represented in this small application? **Assumption:** The application supports demonstrable active sessions so that all-session sign-out can be tested, without prescribing session storage or authentication technology.
- **Question (non-blocking):** How is “per account per hour” applied to nonexistent identifiers and where do hour boundaries fall? **Assumption:** Limit attempts by submitted account identifier without exposing account existence; do not prescribe a fixed or rolling window beyond the standard's one-hour limit.
- **Question (non-blocking):** What delivery format/channel is intended for reset links and owner notices? **Assumption:** The required in-memory sink makes the demo's issued recovery messages and successful-reset notices observable; no real mail/SMS service is assumed.
- **Question (non-blocking):** Which other production limitations should be documented? **Assumption:** At minimum document the two evidenced demo limitations (synthetic accounts and in-memory notifications); add further limitations only if supported by the implementation.
- **Assumption:** The complete pinned story has no end marker to copy; the attachment reader exposed no image contents or acceptance marker. No approved earlier outputs are available.
